$comment: The fleet's self-description. Every tag here is a DECLARATION by a deployed resource about itself, which is why deploy.py keeps no list of 122 lambdas and reset_dev.py keeps no list of tables. Prose on why each exists is in AGENTS.md; the enums live here so a reader gets them in one look and a lint reads the same values it documents. Descriptions are data, not comments: `jq '."gerp:layer".values | keys'` answers the question.

gerp:src-dir.purpose: where this function's code is, exactly — so a deployed name never has to follow a naming convention
gerp:src-dir.value: the source dir, repo-relative: modules/<m>/lambdas/<fn> or prod/<stack>/lambdas/<fn>

consumers.scripts/deploy.py: fleet membership + fn -> src_dir in one query; fans update-function-code over the result
consumers.modules/aws/aws.py: PROPOSED — resolve a deployed name to its handler for in-process dispatch, instead of globbing the name's last segment (which collides: apply_inbound, settle_agreement)

notes: presence is fleet membership; a lambda deployed as an image rather than a zip omits the tag
merge with an existing tags map, never replace it

gerp:layer.purpose: what class of state this holds, so a reset knows what it may empty

values.config: schema / settings / rules-params. Platform configuration — NEVER reset.
values.books: the accounting ledger and everything derived from it: balances, pending, report CSVs
values.operational: the business registers — inventory, invoicing, purchasing, labor, contacts, assets, shipping, tasks, notes, calendar, inbox, payments, treasury — plus rule instances and agent uploads
values.session: agent chat / email / session state: transcripts, the S3SessionManager store, memory

consumers.scripts/reset_dev.py: empties every layer but config; --layer <name> targets one
consumers.tests/helpers/localaws.py: snapshot_schemas() sweeps by this tag and describe_table()s each hit into tests/testdata/table-schemas.json
consumers.the local image: PROPOSED — seed what a stack needs, reset between scenarios

gerp:layer.query: aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=gerp:layer --resource-type-filters dynamodb:table s3:bucket
notes: the reset EMPTIES, never drops — table/stream config and bucket policies survive, so the tenant stays functional with empty books
AgentCore Memory is neither DDB nor S3, so `session` clears the saved-chat index and session store while Memory transcripts age out on TTL

gerp:stack.purpose: which local image this resource belongs to, so standing one up is a query rather than a hand-kept list
gerp:stack.one_owner_per_resource: A resource carries exactly ONE stack — the one that OWNS it. Cross-stack reads are a fact about the stack, declared in depends_on below, not a second value on every resource. The four operator tables are read by bff and written by tower; they are tagged platform.

init_customer.description: the part of a tenant that OUTLIVES the tenant — the document store, its CMK, the export reader role and export_gerp. A separate stack because a statefile is terraform's only destroy boundary: closing a gerp destroys per_customer whole while the owner's export stays downloadable for fifteen days. Applied first at provisioning, destroyed last at the end of that window.

per_customer.description: a tenant's own stack — a composition of modules/*/infra, which is why prod/per_customer/ declares almost nothing and the directory cannot answer membership. Finds init_customer's bucket and CMK by NAME with data sources, not remote state.

bff.description: gradienterp.cloud, the owner web app. Reads platform's four operator tables and invokes tower's provisioner — both are depends_on, which is what merges their function config into the bff's local image.

openlyoperated_biz.description: the public dashboard: static site plus its read API. Two roots, one stack.

platform.description: operator singletons — the customers/members/accounts/profiles tables, the shared gerp-events bus, the event dispatcher. Not a front door; the substrate the other three read.

tower.description: provisioning, billing, signup intake. A runtime with no front door of its own.

optimizer.description: the a2a hub and the profile-match index

not_tagged.aws_lambda_function_url: a property of its function, not an independent resource — the function's tag covers it and the builder reads get_function_url_config. Three of the four front doors in this fleet are Function URLs and appear in no OpenAPI export.
not_tagged.routes: an APIGW route is not tagged. The gateway already merges routes across every module that attached one, and exports them: aws apigatewayv2 export-api --specification OAS30. Websocket APIs cannot be exported (OAS does not model them) — read those with get-routes.

gerp:stack.applied_via: provider default_tags, one block per terraform root (prod/*/versions.tf) — NOT per resource. Every resource a root creates carries it, including inside child modules and including resources added later, so there is nothing to forget and no lint needed for presence. Untaggable types (aws_apigatewayv2_route) simply do not receive it.

consumers.the local image: PROPOSED — one query returns a stack's resource set, so standing it up needs no hand-kept list
